Huntley College of Agriculture College of Business Administration College of Education and Integrative Studies College of Engineering College of Environmental Design College of Letters, Arts, and Social Sciences College of Science The Collins College of Hospitality Management College of Professional and Global Education University Library Student Programs for Support and Enrichment Centers and Institutes University Interdisciplinary Programs Index of Courses Index of Academic Programs Index of Roadmaps Index of Academic Colleges, Departments, and Programs University Administration, Regulations, and History Directory Archived Catalog PDFs My Portfolio Add to My Favorites (opens a new window) Share this Page Facebook this Page (opens a new window) Tweet this Page (opens a new window) Print (opens a new window) Help (opens a new window) 2026-2027 University Catalog Kinesiology and Health Promotion Department Building 66 Room 213 | (909) 869-2768 | Department Website | Faculty Directory The Kinesiology and Health Promotion (KHP) Department mission is to educate, mentor, and inspire students through scientific inquiry and hands‑on learning. The KHP Department emphasizes scientific inquiry and experiential learning grounded in curiosity, integrity, collaboration, inclusivity, and innovation-values central to our strategic plan. The strategic objective of the department is to investigate ways to advance the art of science of health and human movment. It offers a Bachelor of Science alongside a Master of Science. Faculty engage in cutting‑edge research-including postural analysis, neuromechanical control of movement, aging, human performance optimization, athlete transitions, fitness technologies and behavior modification, athlete activism, health outcomes, adapted physical education, cultural competency, emotional health and wellbeing, physical activity and public health. Students benefit from robust facilities, including our state of the art exercise science laboratory, which support both undergraduate and graduate instruction and research. The department fosters cross‑disciplinary engagement while preparing students for teaching, clinical, allied health, corporate wellness, sport industry, and public health roles. The KHP Club and the Pre‑PT/OT are two student clubs serving our undergraduate students. Programs Bachelor Kinesiology, B.S. - General Subplan/Option: 120 units Kinesiology, B.S. - Physical Education Teacher Education Subplan/Option: 120 units Master Kinesiology, M.S. - Adapted Physical Education

courses.title: Basketball Activity
courses.description: Instruction in basketball skills, techniques, rules, offensive and defensive strategies, and team play. May be taken unlimited times.

courses.title: Softball Activity
courses.description: Instruction in the skills, strategies and rules of slow-pitch softball including offensive and defensive strategies and team play.

courses.title: Soccer Activity
courses.description: Instruction in the skills, strategies and rules of soccer including offensive and defensive strategies and team play. May be taken unlimited times.

courses.title: Volleyball Activity
courses.description: Basic fundamentals of volleyball including the serve, passing, spiking, offensive and defensive strategies, rules, and team play. May be taken unlimited times.

courses.title: Ultimate Frisbee Activity
courses.description: Instruction in the skills, strategies and rules of Ultimate Frisbee. Emphasis of the offensive and defensive skills and strategies needed for team play and the importance of sportsmanship. May be taken unlimited times.

courses.title: Introduction to Wheelchair Basketball Activity
courses.description: Introduction to the fundamentals and techniques of wheelchair basketball. Emphasis on skill development in chair mobility, dribbling, passing, shooting, defensive positioning, and team strategies. Learn the history, rules, and etiquette of wheelchair basketball while developing physical fitness, teamwork, and understanding of inclusive sport participation.

courses.title: Archery Activity
courses.description: Instruction in the basic techniques, principles and skills involved in recreational and competitive archery including safety precautions, proper form, scoring, and history of the sport. May be taken unlimited times.

courses.title: Swimming Activity
courses.description: Basic swimming and safety skills. Safety skills include treading water, survival float, and general pool safety. Orientations to the water, floating, front and back kicking, arm strokes, and rhythmic breathing. Underwater, distance swimming, swim relays may be applied. May be taken unlimited times.

courses.title: Intermediate/Advanced Archery Activity
courses.description: Advanced instruction in archery, focusing on refining techniques, enhancing precision, and developing competitive strategies. Topics include advanced shooting form, equipment tuning, mental conditioning, tournament preparation, and adaptive techniques for various archery disciplines. Emphasis on safety, consistency and performance optimization for recreational and competitive archers.
courses.prerequisites: KIN 1200A or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Badminton Activity
courses.description: Instruction and skill development of badminton including racket handling, footwork/court positioning, serves, forehand and backhand overheads, clears, drops, drives, smash and strategies for doubles and singles game playing. May be taken unlimited times.

courses.title: Tennis Activity
courses.description: Instruction and skill development of tennis including the following strokes: forehand and backhand groundstrokes, forehand and backhand volleys, lobs, overhead smash and the serve. The readiness position, racket grips, court etiquette, game rules and game scoring will also be presented. May be taken unlimited times.

courses.title: Pickleball Activity
courses.description: Instruction and skill development of pickleball including the following strokes: forehand and backhand groundstrokes, volley, serve and dink. The readiness position, paddle grips, court etiquette, game history and rules and game scoring will also be presented.

courses.title: Social Dance Activity
courses.description: Knowledge and instruction in social/ballroom dancing, and skill development for dances such as line dancing, country western, waltz, swing, and selected Latin dances. May be taken unlimited times.

courses.title: Aikido Activity
courses.description: Aikido is a Japanese martial art of self-defense that has effective control of the unprovoked attack as its central objective. The course will emphasize attainment of basic Aikido skills. May be taken unlimited times.

courses.title: Karate Activity
courses.description: Principles of various styles of karate with emphasis on Okinowan style. Appropriate for all proficiency levels and martial arts styles. May be taken unlimited times.

courses.title: Self-Defense Activity
courses.description: Instruction and skill development in Matrix self-defense patterns. Course emphasizes response to physical threat and attacks and rape prevention for women. Legal factors, personal safety awareness, and management of assaultive behaviors.

courses.title: Circuit Training Activity
courses.description: Full body conditioning or resistance training using high-intensity stations. Each station targets certain muscles and can be modified for every fitness level, which can improve strength and muscular endurance as well as promote cardiorespiratory conditioning. May be taken unlimited times.

courses.title: Jogging Activity
courses.description: Participation in jogging or walking exercise to develop and maintain cardiorespiratory fitness. Involves the instruction and practice in the techniques of jogging and power-walking as well as information on the health benefits of these activities. May be taken unlimited times.

courses.title: Kickboxing Activity
courses.description: Instruction and performance of cardiovascular activities utilizing various moves from martial arts, boxing and kickboxing. The main goal of the class is cardiovascular fitness. Variable levels of intensity are included. May be taken unlimited times.

courses.title: Step Aerobics Activity
courses.description: Concepts and performance of aerobic exercise utilizing a step apparatus of various heights to regulate exercise intensity levels. Includes fitness and nutrition, concepts for healthier living. May be taken unlimited times.

courses.title: Stretching Activity
courses.description: A stretching program designed to increase flexibility and core strength, improve posture and balance, and reduce muscle tension and low-back pain. May be taken unlimited times.

courses.title: Yoga and Meditation Activity
courses.description: Concepts and performance of yoga and meditation practices. Cultivation of the union of mind, body and spirit through movement and contemplative practice. Variable levels of yoga as well as the introduction of various meditation practices. May be taken unlimited times.

courses.title: Weight Training Activity
courses.description: Instruction in basic concepts involving the muscular system and its function in weight training exercise. Includes skill development through use of weight-training exercises to develop muscular strength and muscular endurance. May be taken unlimited times.

courses.title: Challenge Ropes Course Activity
courses.description: Challenges on the Cal Poly Pomona Ropes Course. Participation in team building initiatives and learn to facilitate high and low level rope adventure activities. May be taken unlimited times.

courses.title: Special Study for Lower Division Students
courses.description: Individual or group investigation, research, studies, or surveys of selected problems. Proposals to be initiated by student(s) with guidance from faculty. Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Introduction to Kinesiology and Health Promotion
courses.description: Introduction to the discipline, fundamental concepts, theories, history, methods, and research within kinesiology and health promotion.

courses.title: Biomechanics
courses.description: Introduction to basic mechanical and anatomical principles of human movement in sports and exercise. Corequisite(s): KIN 2040L .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 2340 and BIO 2340L .

courses.title: Biomechanics Laboratory
courses.description: Applications of biomechanics concepts to the real world using the laboratory technologies of human measurement and the application of biomechanical principles in human movement analysis. Corequisite(s): KIN 2040 .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 2340 and BIO 2340L .

courses.title: Applied Health and Well-Being
courses.description: This course addresses the issues pertaining to health behaviors including theory of behavior change, dimensions of health and wellness (e.g., mental, physical, environmental, social) and health communication.

courses.title: Health and Well-Being
courses.description: Issues pertaining to stress management, mind/body health, interpersonal relationships, sexual health, fitness, nutrition, behavioral modification, and consumer health.

courses.title: Movement Education for Diverse Populations
courses.description: Introduction to the fundamental dimensions of an effective movement educator needed by all kinesiology and health promotion majors. Key aspects of effective teaching and learning are explored (e.g., teaching styles, feedback, demonstrations, assessment, cultural competency).

courses.title: Introduction to Physical Education Teacher Education
courses.description: Prospective teachers are introduced to current practices in planning and teaching lessons, teacher behaviors, teacher qualifications, professional development, and career opportunities in physical education.

courses.title: Standards and Assessment
courses.description: Development of the skills and knowledge necessary to effectively create and administer various forms of standards-based assessment in K-12 general and adapted physical education settings. The focus is on creating engaging lessons, developing effective assessments, and collecting data to monitor student progress and growth.

courses.title: Sport, Race and Social Justice
courses.description: Examines the intersection between sport, race, power, and oppression. Use social justice framework to explore how the structure, values, and practices of U.S. sport have constructed, reproduced, and challenged problematic racial ideologies.

courses.title: Contemporary Issues in Health and Human Movement
courses.description: Contemporary sociocultural issues pertaining to health and human movement. It critically explores how diversity appears in the field of kinesiology and health promotion.
courses.prerequisites: Kinesiology major.

courses.title: Introduction to Sport and Social Justice
courses.description: Utilization of a social justice framework to examine current and historic events and movements in sport. An intersectional lens will be used to examine sport as a site of social justice and activism.

courses.title: Foundations of Public Health and Applied Epidemiology
courses.description: Introduction to the core dimensions of public health and examines principles of epidemiology as they relate to various public health activities, outcomes, and issues.

courses.title: Foundations of Adapted Physical Activity
courses.description: Introduction to various disability concepts, such as atypical growth, development, and motor functions, legal mandates, and models of disability/inclusion. Particular focus will be placed on adapted movements for maximum inclusion. Corequisite(s): KIN 2460AS .
courses.prerequisites: Kinesiology major.

courses.title: Stress Management for Healthy Living
courses.description: A holistic approach to stress management; preventing and/or alleviating physical symptoms of stress; exploration of the mind/body connection.

courses.title: Special Topics for Lower Division Students
courses.description: Group study of a selected well-defined topic or area not covered by a regularly offered course.

courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units applicable to a degree, with a maximum of 2 sections per semester.

courses.title: Foundations of Exercise Science
courses.description: [GE 5D] Scientific aspects of exercise science, biological systems associated with human performance and function, metabolic determinants of energy expenditure, nutrition in sport and weight control, physiological function in extreme environments; applications of technology to exercise; performance enhancing aids; exercise and disease prevention.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Exercise Physiology
courses.description: Aerobic and anaerobic energy sources for muscular activity, neuromuscular physiology and function, and cardiopulmonary/respiratory physiology and function as it relates to exercise. Examples include physiological and metabolic adaptations to resistance and endurance training, nutritional and ergogenic aspects of human performance, environmental impact on exercise performance, and hormonal response to exercise. Corequisite(s): KIN 3030L .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 2350 and BIO 2350L .

courses.title: Exercise Physiology Laboratory
courses.description: Test and measure human performance including anaerobic and aerobic capacity, muscular kinematics, biometrics, and body composition. Corequisite(s): KIN 3030 .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 2350 and BIO 2350L .

courses.title: Elementary Physical Education
courses.description: Provides opportunities to explore skills and methods for teaching elementary physical education. Emphasis on standards based physical education activities with the use of Physical Education Model Content Standards for California Public Schools. Corequisite(s): KIN 3100A .
courses.prerequisites: KIN 2220 , KIN 2230 , and KIN 2460 /AS, or permission of the instructor.

courses.title: Elementary Physical Education Activity
courses.description: Demonstrate skills and methods for teaching elementary physical education. Emphasis on standards based physical education activities with the use of Physical Education Model Content Standards for California Public Schools. Corequisite(s): KIN 3100 .
courses.prerequisites: KIN 2220 , KIN 2230 , and KIN 2460 /AS, or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Secondary Physical Education - 1
courses.description: Application of principles, methods, strategies and practices for teaching fitness, rhythms and dance, gymnastics and self-defense through the integration of the Physical Education Model Content Standards for California Public Schools and California Teacher Performance Expectations.
courses.prerequisites: KIN 2220 - Introduction to Physical Education Teacher Education (3) KIN 2220, KIN 2230, KIN 2460, and KIN 2460AS.

courses.title: Secondary Physical Education-1 Activity
courses.description: Applies principles, methods, strategies and practices for teaching fitness, rhythms and dance, gymnastics and self-defense through the integration of the Physical Education Model Content Standards for California Public Schools and California Teacher Performance Expectations. Corequisite(s): KIN 3110 .
courses.prerequisites: KIN 2220 , KIN 2230 , KIN 2460 , and KIN 2460AS .

courses.title: Secondary Physical Education - 2
courses.description: Identification of principles, methods, strategies, and practices for teaching individual, dual, team, and racket sports through the integration of the Physical Education Model Content Standards for California Public Schools and California Teacher Performance Expectations. Corequisite(s): KIN 3120A .
courses.prerequisites: KIN 2220 , KIN 2230 , and KIN 2460/AS .

courses.title: Secondary Physical Education Activity - 2
courses.description: Application of principles, methods, strategies and practices for teaching individual, dual, team, and racket sports through the integration of the Physical Education Model Content Standards for California Public Schools and California Teacher Performance Expectations. Corequisite(s): KIN 3120 .
courses.prerequisites: KIN 2220 , KIN 2230 , and KIN 2460/AS .

courses.title: Teaching Aquatics
courses.description: Introduction to the safety protocols and strategies to teach beginner to advanced swimming skills in secondary physical education. Corequisite(s): KIN 3130A .
courses.prerequisites: KIN 2220 and KIN 2230 .

courses.title: Teaching Aquatics Activity
courses.description: In-water applications of skills and strategies to teach beginner to advanced swimming skills in secondary physical education. Corequisite(s): KIN 3130 .

courses.title: Outdoor and Adventure Education
courses.description: Provides physical education teacher education (PETE) students with the skills and strategies necessary for creating inclusive outdoor and adventure education activities. Theoretical topics include group facilitation, program design, planning, frontloading and debriefing principles, psychosocial principles, and risk management. Corequisite(s): KIN 3140A .
courses.prerequisites: KIN 2220 - Introduction to Physical Education Teacher Education (3) KIN 2220 , KIN 2230 , KIN 2460 , and KIN 2460AS .

courses.title: Outdoor and Adventure Education Activity
courses.description: Prepares PETE students to design and deliver inclusive outdoor and adventure education. Emphasis placed on facilitation, program design, planning, debriefing, psychosocial principles, and risk management. Includes applied teaching experience by creating, leading, and reflecting on activities, strengthening leadership, instructional practice, and adaptive strategies for physical education. Corequisite(s): KIN 3140 .
courses.prerequisites: KIN 2220 - Introduction to Physical Education Teacher Education (3) KIN 2220 , KIN 2230 , KIN 2460 , and KIN 2460AS .

courses.title: Health Disparities and Social Justice
courses.description: Introduction to concepts of health equity, health disparities, and social justice. It examines how determinants of health impact people’s abilities to engage in healthy lifestyles and evaluates intervention practices used to reduce health disparities in the U.S.
courses.prerequisites: KIN 2400 and SOC 2201 .

courses.title: Applied Adapted Physical Education
courses.description: Evaluation of instructional strategies, assessments, progress monitoring, and behavior management strategies to implement when teaching students with disabilities. Corequisite(s): KIN 3460A .
courses.prerequisites: KIN 2220 - Introduction to Physical Education Teacher Education (3) KIN 2220 , KIN 2230 , KIN 2460 , and KIN 2460AS .

courses.title: Applied Adapted Physical Education Activity
courses.description: Application of supervised clinical teaching of adapted physical education to participants with disabilities at the Cal Poly Pomona Motor Development Clinic (MDC). Students will learn the MDC operational processes. Corequisite(s): KIN 3460 .
courses.prerequisites: KIN 2220 , KIN 2230 , and KIN 2460/AS .
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 4 units, with a maximum of 2 units per semester.

courses.title: Exercise Prescription and Fitness Testing
courses.description: Examines the theoretical and practical exercise prescription and fitness assessments for individuals using the Frequency, Intensity, Time, and Type (FITT) principle. Corequisite(s): KIN 3520A .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 2340 / BIO 2340L and BIO 2350 / BIO 2350L .

courses.title: Exercise Prescription and Fitness Testing Activity
courses.description: Performance of fitness assessments of apparently healthy individuals and prescribe exercise programs using the Frequency, Intensity, Time, and Type (FITT) principle. Corequisite(s): KIN 3520 .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 2340 / BIO 2340L and BIO 2350 / BIO 2350L .

courses.title: Exercise and Health Behavior Modification
courses.description: Consider how individual factors influence health behaviors, motivation, and adherence to lifestyle changes. Emphasizes identifying cardiovascular, pulmonary, and metabolic health risks, and explores how these tools guide safe and effective exercise and health practices. Through applied learning, develop skills in motivational interviewing, evidence-based behavior change models, and effective communication and leadership strategies.
courses.prerequisites: BIO 2350 and BIO 2350L .

courses.title: Research Methods in Health and Human Movement
courses.description: Introduction to basic types of procedures utilized to design and conduct research in health and human movement. Emphasis will be placed on the research process, including relevant research types, designs, methodologies, and analytical approaches.
courses.prerequisites: STA 1200 or STA 1202 , and KIN 2020 .

courses.title: Motor Behavior
courses.description: This course examines typical and atypical motor development, motor control, and motor learning across the lifespan in the context of human movement. 3-hour lecture/discussion. Corequisite(s): KIN 3620A .
courses.prerequisites: Kinesiology major; KIN 2040 , KIN 3030 , or KIN 3040; and KIN 2040L , KIN 3030 L, or KIN 3040L.

courses.title: Motor Behavior Activity
courses.description: This course provides foundational level exposure to typical and atypical motor development, motor control, and motor learning through various activities. One two-hour activity. Corequisite(s): KIN 3620 .
courses.prerequisites: KIN 2040 , KIN 3030 , or KIN 3040; and KIN 2040L , KIN 3030L , or KIN 3040L.

courses.title: Dimensions of the Aging Process
courses.description: Issues pertaining to the quality of life through the aging process, specifically throughout the adult life span, as they relate to kinesiology and health. Socio-cultural, emotional, physical, and health and well-being influences be examined as they impact aging.

courses.title: Stress Management: The Science of Living Well
courses.description: [GE 5D] Explores the impact of science, technology, and culture on human well-being, values, and quality of life. Focuses on the science of stress and its effects on mental health, disease, and illness on an individual and global scale. Examines the application and generalization of basic human biological sciences with an emphasis on psychophysiological responses to stress and evidence-based theories for its reduction. Considers the dichotomy of technological advances, including positive uses of biotechnology and AI programs to manage stress, alongside the detrimental effects of technology saturation and social media on mental health. Investigates the impact and paradox of the science and technology of stress in civilizations over time, including how they have affected human living due to rapid and dramatic development (e.g., global hegemony, human displacement). Explores cultural acceptance and the resultant implications of mental health concerns. Themes are explored mainly through lecture, reading, discussion, and personal exploration of the course content.

courses.title: Special Study for Upper Division Students
courses.description: Individual or group investigation, research, studies, or surveys of selected problems at advanced level. Proposals to be initiated by student(s) with guidance from faculty. Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Applied Biomechanics
courses.description: Examination of the application of the quantitative assessment of human movement. Concepts covered include kinematics (movement), kinetics (forces), and the underlying neuromuscular mechanisms. Corequisite(s): KIN 4040L .
courses.prerequisites: KIN 2040 - Biomechanics (3) KIN 2040 and KIN 2040L .

courses.title: Applied Biomechanics Laboratory
courses.description: Hands-on experience in the quantitative analysis of human movement. Students will collect, process, and interpret biomechanical data using instruments such as motion capture systems, force plates, inertial measurement units (IMUs), and electromyography (EMG). Emphasis is placed on the integration of kinematic, kinetic, and electromyographic data to analyze movement performance and neuromuscular control. Corequisite(s): KIN 4040 .
courses.prerequisites: KIN 2040 and KIN 2040L .

courses.title: Drugs and Society
courses.description: Prescription, over-the-counter and illegal drug use in contemporary society; social, cultural, political, and economic impact of drug use; prevention and treatment of addiction.

courses.title: Movement Anatomy and Evaluation
courses.description: Synthesize the anatomy of the musculoskeletal system, connect the structural anatomy to body movement, and identify clinical assessments to evaluate body movements. Corequisite(s): KIN 4120L .
courses.prerequisites: KIN 2040 or KIN 3040, and KIN 2040L or KIN 3040L.

courses.title: Movement Anatomy and Evaluation Laboratory
courses.description: Analysis of body movements based on structural anatomy and conduct clinical assessments of synovial joints. Corequisite(s): KIN 4120 .
courses.prerequisites: KIN 2040 and KIN 2040L .

courses.title: Physical Education Curriculum and Assessment
courses.description: General guidelines and foundations for curriculum development designed to address the needs of learners in diverse settings. Topics include curriculum construction, planning, implementation, and assessment in elementary and secondary school settings.
courses.prerequisites: KIN 3460, and KIN 3460A or KIN 3460AS; KIN 3100 /KIN 3100A; KIN 3110 /KIN 3110A; KIN 3120 /KIN 3120A; KIN 3130 /KIN 3130A; and KIN 3140 /KIN 3140A.

courses.title: Philosophical and Ethical Issues in Health and Human Movement
courses.description: Utilization of philosophical perspectives to examine ethical issues relevant to health and human movement. Current topics and issues related to physical activity, sport, the body, and health will be examined. A critical examination of ethical issues as they relate to inequity and implicit biases is embedded within the culture of health and human movement. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement.
courses.prerequisites: KHP major and junior or senior standing.

courses.title: Adapted Physical Education Motor Assessment
courses.description: Introduction to motor assessment strategies, policies, and procedures used in adapted physical education, with an emphasis on state and federal mandates. Corequisite(s): KIN 4330AS .
courses.prerequisites: KIN 3460 / KIN 3460A .

courses.title: Adapted Physical Activity Through the Lifespan
courses.description: In-depth exploration of adapted physical activity across the lifespan. Gain a comprehensive understanding of the principles, practices, and challenges associated with designing and implementing physical activity programs for individuals with disabilities. Corequisite(s): KIN 4350A .

courses.title: Adapted Physical Activity Through the Lifespan Activity
courses.description: Apply strategies for an implementation of adapted physical activity across the lifespan. Design and implement adapted physical activity programs for individuals with disabilities of all ages. Corequisite(s): KIN 4350 .

courses.title: Internship in Kinesiology
courses.description: On-the-job training and work experience in kinesiology or health promotion under the guidance of a faculty internship coordinator and on-site job supervisor. The internship is arranged by the student and may not be a continuation of an ongoing job or volunteer experience. A minimum of 8 hours per week (120 hours/semester) per unit credit.
courses.prerequisites: Upper division or graduate standing.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 4 units.

courses.title: Inequality in Sport and Physical Activity
courses.description: [GE 4C] Social inequality is investigated through the lens of sport and physical activity. Social science theories of inequality are applied to empirical examples in sport and physical activity. Explanations for inequality, critiques, and possibilities for change are examined.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Social and Historical Perspectives in Kinesiology
courses.description: Social and historical perspectives on kinesiology and sport from Colonial period to the present in the United States. Historical and contemporary physical activity, sport, physical education, and exercise are investigated as they shaped and shape American culture. Emphasizes theoretical and applied approaches to addressing issues around race, gender, sexuality, disability, social class and their relationship to sport and physical activity both socially and historically.

courses.title: Sport, Media, and Social Justice
courses.description: [GE 4C] Utilization of a social justice framework to examine the symbiotic relationship between sport and media. Theoretical and methodological insights from kinesiology, sociology, history, ethnic and women’s studies, and anthropology will be used to explore how sport and media reproduce and challenge dominant Western socio-cultural perspectives.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: US Sport, Culture, and Social Justice
courses.description: [GE 4C] Utilization of a social justice framework to examine the relationship between sport, culture, and US society. Theoretical and methodological insights from sociology, history, ethnic and women’s studies, media studies, queer studies, anthropology, and kinesiology will be used to examine the role of sport in US culture. A primary focus will be on the ways in which the structure and culture of US sport have constructed, reproduced, and challenged discriminatory values, ideologies, and practices.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Electrocardiography in Health and Exercise
courses.description: Theoretical and practical techniques for analyzing and recognizing normal and abnormal electrocardiography (ECG). Understanding of ECG through an appreciation of the mechanisms of cardiac activation in health and exercise. Corequisite(s): KIN 4500L .
courses.prerequisites: KIN 303 or KIN 3030 ; KIN 303L or KIN 3030L .

courses.title: Electrocardiography in Health and Exercise Laboratory
courses.description: Practical application and techniques for analyzing and recognizing normal and abnormal electrocardiography (ECG) through laboratory experiences of the mechanisms of cardiac activation in health and exercise. Corequisite(s): KIN 4500 .
courses.prerequisites: KIN 303 or KIN 3030 ; KIN 303L or KIN 3030L .

courses.title: Sport Injury and Illness
courses.description: Examines current topics in sport injury and illness prevention as they affect health and human performance. Corequisite(s): KIN 4530A .

courses.title: Sport Injury and Illness Activity
courses.description: Application of therapeutic techniques and emergency procedures for common sports injuries and illnesses. Corequisite(s): KIN 4530 .

courses.title: Exercise Bioenergetics and Metabolism
courses.description: Biochemical properties and regulation of metabolic pathways related to production and utilization of cellular energy, especially in human skeletal muscle and adipose tissue during various exercise and nutritional conditions. Metabolism and nutritional aspects of human performance and weight-control.
courses.prerequisites: KIN 3030 and KIN 3030L .

courses.title: Principles of Strength and Conditioning
courses.description: Provides the knowledge and skills to apply strength and conditioning principles for the enhancement of human performance. Includes learning advanced exercise techniques, program design, and performance assessment procedures. Corequisite(s): KIN 4550L
courses.prerequisites: KIN 3030 and KIN 3030L .

courses.title: Principles of Strength and Conditioning Laboratory
courses.description: Assessments of muscular fitness and apply training techniques for optimal athletic performance. Corequisite(s): KIN 4550 .
courses.prerequisites: KIN 3030 /L.

courses.title: Motor Learning and Control
courses.description: Examination of theories which underlie the acquisition and control of human movement. The process of acquisition and control of highly skilled movements that lead to permanent gains in performance is emphasized.
courses.prerequisites: KIN 2040 or KIN 3040, KIN 2040L or KIN 3040L, and KIN 3620 / KIN 3620A .

courses.title: Sport Psychology
courses.description: Focus on relevant theoretical and empirical perspectives for topics related to sport psychology. Emphasis will be placed on evaluating various aspects of sport psychology and the broader psychosocial role of sport in society.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing.

courses.title: Exercise Prescription and Fitness Testing for Diverse Populations
courses.description: Examination of the theoretical and practical exercise prescription and fitness assessment considerations for diverse populations such as youth, older adults, pregnant women, persons with chronic health conditions, and individuals with disabilities.
courses.prerequisites: KIN 3520 / KIN 3520A .

courses.title: Senior Project
courses.description: Selection and completion of a project under faculty supervision. Topic is typical of problems, which may confront graduates in future employment or graduate study. Formal report may be required depending on project.
courses.prerequisites: Senior standing.

courses.title: Physical Education Teacher Education Capstone
courses.description: Capstone course for physical education teacher education (PETE) students. Designed to prepare PETE students for clinical practice and teaching physical education in California public schools.
courses.prerequisites: KIN 3100 KIN 3110 , KIN 3120 , KIN 3130 , KIN 3140 , and KIN 3460 / KIN 3460A .

courses.title: Intervention Design and Evaluation
courses.description: Explores the process of developing, implementing, and evaluating public health interventions. Examines different program settings, including schools, worksites, communities, and clinics. Corequisite(s): KIN 4650A .
courses.prerequisites: Upper division standing and KIN 3600 .

courses.title: Intervention Design and Evaluation Activity
courses.description: The process of developing, implementing, and evaluating public health interventions. Students will select a population of interest, health outcome and program setting. In response to their health outcome, they will conduct a needs assessment, develop and implement an intervention and evaluate its success. Corequisite(s): KIN 4650 .
courses.prerequisites: Upper division standing and KIN 3600 .

courses.title: Emotional Wellbeing and Stress Prevention
courses.description: [GE 4C] Underscores, through a scientific lens, the idea that stress and impaired emotional health are diseases that contribute to real-world individual and societal problems. From an integrative and interdisciplinary perspective, it looks at the mind body connection regarding stress and mental health through various biological sciences and incorporates biotechnology as a way of examining and improving mental and emotional health. Addresses how mental health influences and is influenced by cultural values and social norms, and it explores how unresolved emotional stress can lead to medical challenges, problematic personal and social behaviors, and broad social problems. It proposes a solution of scientific understanding of the mind/body connection, and the application of biotechnology and appropriate cultural approaches to manage stress and improve mental, emotional, and social health.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Special Study for Graduate Students
courses.description: Individual or group investigation, research, studies, or surveys of selected problems at graduate level. Proposals to be initiated by student(s) with guidance from faculty. Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Adapted Physical Education Behavior Intervention and Support Plans
courses.description: Introduction to various instructional strategies of behavior management. Attention will be paid to the Adapted Physical Education (APE) Teacher’s role in the development of Individualized Education Programs (IEP) and behavior intervention plans. Learn positive behavior intervention strategies to facilitate integrated APE services based on individual students’ motor needs. Corequisite(s): KIN 5320A .
courses.prerequisites: KIN 3460 , KIN 3460A , and post-baccalaureate standing, graduate standing, or consent of the instructor.

courses.title: Adapted Physical Education Behavior Intervention and Support Plans Activity
courses.description: Applies positive behavior intervention strategies to facilitate integrated APE services based on individual students’ motor needs. Collaboration with members of an Individualized Education Programs (IEP) team to develop, implement, and evaluate IEP behavioral intervention plans. Corequisite(s): KIN 5320 .
courses.prerequisites: KIN 3460 ; KIN 3460A ; and post-baccalaureate standing, graduate standing, or permission of the instructor.

courses.title: Adapted Physical Education Program Development
courses.description: Introduction to concepts of program development for implementing Adapted Physical Education (APE) Service Delivery Models to a variety of disabilities from childhood to adulthood as guided by the California APE guidelines. Corequisite(s): KIN 5340AS.
courses.prerequisites: KIN 4330 , KIN 4330AS , KIN 5320 , and KIN 5320AS.

courses.title: Adapted Physical Education Program Implementation Activity
courses.description: The concepts of program development for implementing APE Service Delivery Models to a variety of disabilities from childhood to adulthood as guided by the California APE guidelines. Corequisite(s): KIN 5340 .
courses.prerequisites: KIN 4330 , KIN 4330AS , KIN 5320 , and KIN 5320A .

courses.title: Transition Planning in Adapted Physical Education
courses.description: Focuses on developing the essential knowledge and collaborative skills to create effective Individualized Transition Plans (ITP) in Adapted Physical Education for students with diverse abilities. Corequisite(s): KIN 5350AS.
courses.prerequisites: KIN 3460S; KIN 3460AS; and post-baccalaureate standing, graduate standing, or consent of the instructor

courses.title: Transition Planning in Adapted Physical Education Activity
courses.description: The essential knowledge and collaborative skills to create effective Individualized Transition Plans (ITP) in Adapted Physical Education for students with diverse abilities. Corequisite(s): KIN 5350 .
courses.prerequisites: KIN 3460 , KIN 3460A ; and post-baccalaureate standing, graduate standing, or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Adapted Physical Education Candidate Assessment
courses.description: Candidates complete the requirement of the Adapted Physical Education (APE) portfolio, that reflects the California Commission on Teacher Credentialing (CCTC) requirements of the Added Authorization standards. Students will also provide evidence of a minimum of 180 hours of APE clinical practice. At the successful completion of the portfolio, candidates will be recommended for the CCTC Adapted Physical Education Added Authorization. Corequisite(s): EDU 5270 or EDU 5260 .
courses.prerequisites: KIN 2460 , KIN 3130 , KIN 3130A , KIN 3460 , KIN 3460A , KIN 4330 , KIN 4330AS , KIN 5320 , KIN 5320AS, KIN 5340 , KIN 5340AS, KIN 5350 , and KIN 5350AS; acceptance into the APE Added Authorization program; approved clinical practice application; resolution of any outstanding Statement of Concern issues arising during APE coursework (if applicable); and post-baccalaureate standing, graduate standing, or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Community-Engaged Practice
courses.description: Introduces principles of evidence-based community-engaged practice in health and human movement. Topics may include community engagement in research, community-based methods, and strategies for establishing and sustaining partnerships with community stakeholders.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.title: School- and Community-based Program Development and Implementation
courses.description: The design of effective programs within school- and community-based settings. Topics cover the principles of program design and implementation, troubleshooting common challenges, and program evaluation.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Physical Education Leadership and Advocacy
courses.description: Knowledge and skills needed to become effective leaders in the field of physical education. Explore various leadership theories, principles, and practices to advocate for the needs of the field of physical education.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Adapted Physical Education Program Leadership
courses.description: Develop knowledge of Adapted Physical Education program administration, funding, and evaluation. Attention will be given to developing students’ use of assisted technology, and enhancing their leadership, advocacy, and interpersonal skills. Corequisite(s): KIN 5750AS .
courses.prerequisites: KIN 4330 , KIN 4330AS , KIN 5320 , and KIN 5320AS; and graduate standing or consent of the instructor.

courses.title: Biomechanical Instrumentation
courses.description: Advanced biomechanical concepts and tools to analyze health and human movement and understand the complex interactions between forces, muscle groups, joints and movement patterns. The latest research on human performance.
courses.prerequisites: KIN 2040 and KIN 2040L , or undergraduate biomechanics course; and graduate standing.

courses.title: Advanced Exercise Physiology
courses.description: The mechanisms underpinning physiological adaptations to resistance and endurance training as well as skeletal muscle bioenergetics and fatigue. Emphasis will be placed on mastering competencies in assessing and analyzing physiological markers of health and human performance.
courses.prerequisites: KIN 3030 and KIN 3030L , or equivalent; and graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Advanced Exercise Physiology Laboratory
courses.description: Laboratory experiments that include human bioenergetics of active skeletal muscle and maintenance of energy homeostasis; neuroendocrine regulation of lipid, carbohydrate, and protein metabolism during exercise and training. Anaerobic and aerobic metabolism during exercise will be measured including mechanisms underlying cardiovascular, pulmonary and skeletal muscle adaptations to divergent exercise training modes. Thermoregulation in heat and cold during exercise and the effects of altitude training adaptations will be studied. Corequisite(s): KIN 5830 .
courses.prerequisites: KIN303 or KIN 3030 ; KIN 303L or KIN 3030L or equivalent.

courses.title: Applied Exercise Testing and Interpretation
courses.description: Application of principles of exercise prescription for apparently healthy populations with medically controlled conditions. Topics include, but are not limited to: preparticipation health screening, graded exercise tests, exercise electrocardiography, motor skill-related assessments, and body composition assessment.
courses.prerequisites: KIN 3030 and KIN 3030L , or equivalent; and graduate standing or consent of the instructor.

courses.title: Advanced Topics in Sports Medicine and Nutrition
courses.description: Contemporary topics in sports medicine and nutrition in relations to sport and exercise. Topics include musculoskeletal, cardiorespiratory, and immunological health in sport and exercise, nutritional and metabolic integration in human performance, ergogenic aids, female athlete triad, sports anemia, and environmental issues in sport and exercise. Special topic concerning women, elderly, and children will be covered. May be taken unlimited times.
courses.prerequisites: KIN 683 and KIN 683L, or KIN 5830 ; and Unconditional Graduate standing.

courses.title: Applied Inquiry and Research Design
courses.description: Introduction to Kinesiology and Health Promotion research through the critical examination of literature and application of key principles, culminating in the design and development of a research proposal. Topics include: theoretical and technical facets of planning and performing research, crafting research questions, research ethics and methodologies.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Data Literacy, Analysis, and Synthesis
courses.description: Exploration of key data and analytical model concepts in Kinesiology and Health Promotion research, culminating in the design, development and implementation of a full research proposal. Topics include: applied research methods, statistical and qualitative analytical methods, analytical software, interpretation of results, data synthesis, and pilot evaluation.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Critical Analysis of Research
courses.description: Critical evaluation of health and human movement literature to promote and broaden student understanding of research within our field. Emphasis is placed on developing an interdisciplinary understanding through an active-learning pedagogy approach.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or consent of the instructor.

courses.title: Research Colloquium
courses.description: Strategies used to disseminate health and human movement research to academic and non-academic audiences. Content includes research presentations and skill-based workshops. Emphasis is placed on developing an interdisciplinary understanding of the field through an active-learning pedagogy approach.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 2 units, with a maximum of 1 unit per semester.

courses.title: Practicing Professional Competencies
courses.description: Provides students with the knowledge and skills needed to advance their career goals. Emphasis will be placed on developing the professional competencies required to be model, dynamic, and adaptable leaders in the Kinesiology and Health Promotion field.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Practicing Pedagogical Competencies
courses.description: Provides students an opportunity to participate in a supportive community of practice. Emphasis will be placed on developing the pedagogical competencies required to be model, inclusive, and adaptable educators in health and human movement. Corequisite(s): Employment as a KHP Graduate Teaching Associate.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing and KIN 5940 .
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 3 units, with a maximum of 1 unit per semester.

courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing.

courses.description: Individual research in a specialized area, under the direction of a graduate faculty member; work does not pertain directly to the thesis. Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Independent Research
courses.description: Individual study/investigation and research in a specialized area proposed by the student with the approval, and under the supervision, of a graduate faculty member; work does not pertain directly to the thesis. Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Master’s Degree Project
courses.description: The Kinesiology and Health Promotion project is the translation of empirical evidence to create and defend an applied artifact relevant to the chosen field of practice. The finished product evidences originality, critical and independent thinking, appropriate organization and format, and thorough documentation.
courses.prerequisites: KIN 5900 and KIN 5910 with an average grade of B or better, KIN 5920 , and KIN 5930 .
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 2 units applicable to a degree, with a maximum of 1 unit per semester

courses.title: Master’s Degree Thesis
courses.description: The Kinesiology and Health Promotion thesis is the written product and oral defense of a systematic study of a significant problem. The finished product evidences originality, critical and independent thinking, appropriate organization and format, and thorough documentation.
courses.prerequisites: KIN 5900 and KIN 5910 with a B grade or better, KIN 5920 , and KIN 5930 .
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 2 or 6 units applicable to a degree, with a maximum of 1 or 3 units per semester; dependent on curriculum year.

courses.title: Master’s Degree Comprehensive Exams
courses.description: The Kinesiology and Health Promotion Comprehensive Exams are an assessment of the student’s ability to integrate the knowledge of the area, show critical and independent thinking, and demonstrate a mastery of the subject matter. The assessments consist of three elements: 1) critical analysis presentation; 2) written exams; and 3) oral defense.
courses.prerequisites: KIN 5910 , KIN 5920 , and KIN 5930 .
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 2 units applicable to a degree, with a maximum of 1 unit per semester.

courses.title: Master’s Degree Continuation
courses.description: Enrollment in this course allows candidates that have enrolled in the maximum number of thesis or project units to maintain resident status in order to receive university services.
